method: Current base and research records deduplicated by record ID. Point-anchor membership in overlapping editorial rectangles; line routes excluded. Local means named non-overlay occupation, occurrence or site event, not a verified habitation census. Distinct location IDs, not repeated phases, drive sparse coverage ranking. Unknown dates are separate and cannot fill dated cells. Broad windows may overlap many cells without continuous presence. Population-known requires numeric population bounds and an associated sourced claim. Language coverage requires an explicit linguistics claim with supporting source. Rows and periods overlap and are not additive. Zero never implies human absence. Early peopling/habitability screen is editorial, not a new arrival chronology. Pending intake not counted as integrated.

items.title: Northern Interior West languages and named enemies
items.reason: Modern linguistic classifications do not date ancient speech before 500 CE. No directly supported named opposing tribes or wars were found in accessed regional sources.

items.title: Pilgrim stone circles, Helen Lookingbill, Hatwai and Hetrick
items.reason: Retained as original-report leads. Accessed metadata and search descriptions do not yet establish independently checked local calendar phases; neither seventy-one circles nor thousands of artifacts is resident population.

items.title: Silver Zone individual scatters
items.reason: Complex has one approximate anchor; survey-level individual points and direct feature dates remain unresolved.

items.title: Wewukiyepuh calendar date
items.reason: Uploaded table says cal BP but narrative says BP. Accessed original abstract lacks calibration; calendar admission withheld.

items.title: Last Supper Cave later interpretation
items.reason: 2015 explicit sample windows retained with calibration version. Later 2024 reanalysis is a lead for revising context; no continuous Early Holocene occupation inferred.

items.title: Interior West material sourcing and diets beyond checked records
items.reason: Sterling, Osprey Beach, Fishing Bridge, Braden/DeMoss and remote Hopewell connections remain bibliographic leads pending original scope and phase verification.

items.title: Earliest Aleutian arrival at 10000 BCE
items.reason: Query span is not settlement evidence. No 10000 BCE settlement admitted; rounded 9000-years-ago synthesis not forced into a new site-specific calendar date.

items.title: Neo-Aleut immigration around 1000 BP
items.reason: West 2019 recalibration supplies substantially later specific mortuary markers. Morphological categories, burials and ancestry do not establish a single population-replacement event.

items.title: Aleutian site grand total
items.reason: No archipelago-wide inventory total verified. Survey and burial-sample counts are not combined as settlements or population.

items.title: Continuous Aleutian settlement
items.reason: Presence in a poorly sampled interval challenges a hiatus but does not prove continuous occupation of every island.

items.title: Genetics as language history
items.reason: No campsite language inferred from genetics or modern language geography; existing model context not duplicated.

items.title: kiribati
items.reason: No island-specific original calibrated sequence verified. Atoll emergence and modern ancestry do not date local occupation; Te Bakoa remains in original BP units.

items.title: kiribati
items.reason: Original Anderson et al. 2000 full text inaccessible; later institutional and genetic introductions repeat differing summaries. Do not select a convenient window. Phoenix monograph catalogue metadata alone does not substantiate its locality dates.

items.title: kiribati
items.reason: Modern maternal-lineage modeling, another island’s crops, and broad dispersal models are not direct settlement dates for a Kiribati island. Petersen/Kirch 2019/Choice citation is bibliographically mixed and not accepted as original excavation evidence.

items.title: nuku-hiva
items.reason: 2022 paper discusses Moetai and other Anaho chronology but original site analyses not independently accessed; Eiao and Fatu Hiva exact local archaeological phase dates unresolved. Genomic coalescent estimates are not directly dated first occupations.

items.title: nuku-hiva

items.title: Northern Idaho — early Holocene
items.geographicScope: Pacific Northwest; Idaho requires a finer audit bin.
items.coverageAssessment: Targets the 10,000–6,000 BCE and 6,000–3,000 BCE collection gaps with named river-corridor sites. Wewukiyepuh and Kelly Forks are new locality leads; Cooper’s Ferry already has an Area B record and needs phase-level comparison rather than another counted place.
items.reviewFlags: Separate BP from cal BP and distinct occupation episodes. Older Cooper’s Ferry component dates must not overwrite the existing Area B model. A long site sequence does not establish continuous residence.

items.title: Northern Nevada and Idaho — named sites

items.reviewFlags: Differentiate dated activity/cache evidence from habitation. Never use insect-cache or artifact counts as human population. Check revised Leonard Rockshelter chronology and explicit calibration.

items.title: Kiribati settlement and contacts
